account: Today I read my appointment book and went to the plaza for the ten o'clock market walk. Three townsfolk each said they had no news, and the secretary reported no correspondence or news this morning. Nothing I have directly observed establishes any secret activity. The unusual detail is the secretary's statement that both appointment books are now in the appointments chest: I originally saw only one there and read that original. I do not yet know who made the other book or whether its contents differ. Another uncertainty is my three o'clock tea appointment, listed simply as tea with the neighbour at an east-bank dockside cottage, without a name or address. The secretary went to the dockside to identify the host before my one o'clock return for accounts. I followed to clarify the two books and the tea invitation. From near a dockside cottage I called out; both the secretary and someone identified as neighbour heard me, though I cannot currently see either and have not yet heard an answer. This may simply be ordinary appointment-keeping and preparations for tea, but I want to establish the second book's origin and the host's identity before drawing conclusions. I still have lunch at home at noon, accounts at one, tea at three, office at four-thirty, and home at seven.
